title: Eventual real-rootedness conjecture for GKP polynomial sequences
statement:
Let $u,v$ be parameters, let $P$ be the polynomial associated with the sequence, and let $q_n^{u,v}$ be the corresponding polynomial sequence. Assume

$$
|v|+u<0
$$

and

$$
P\bigl(\pm(u+v-2l)\bigr)\ne 0\quad\text{for }l\in\mathbb{N}.
$$

**Eventual real-rootedness conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $n$, every zero of $q_n^{u,v}$ is real.

The conjecture predicts eventual real-rootedness even when $P$ has non-real zeros. A preceding example shows that without the relevant assumption, the associated polynomials can have non-real zeros for every $n$; the source gives no resolution of this conjecture.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06578

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).
source_name: Antonio J. Durán, Mario Pérez and Juan L. Varona, “Zeros of GKP sequences of polynomials”, arXiv:2607.06578 (2026).
